title: Triangle Properties: Angles and Side Lengths
seo_title: Grade 6 Triangle Properties Worksheets: Angle Sum and Side Lengths (TEKS 6.8A, STAAR)
standard_text: 6.8A extend previous knowledge of triangles and their properties to include the sum of angles of a triangle, the relationship between the lengths of sides and measures of angles in a triangle, and determining when three lengths form a triangle
meta_desc: Free Grade 6 triangle worksheets for Texas TEKS 6.8A: angle sum of a triangle, missing angles, triangle side lengths, possible third sides and largest angle versus longest side. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Angles add to 180°; the two shorter sides must add to more than the longest.
key_sub: The largest angle is across from the longest side.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • The three angles of every triangle add to 180°.
  • Three lengths make a triangle only if the two shorter sides add to more than the longest side.
  • The third side must be longer than the difference and shorter than the sum of the other two sides.
  • The largest angle is across from the longest side; the smallest angle is across from the shortest side.

Examples

Example

Angles 48° and 75°. Find the third.

48 + 75 = 123

180 − 123

Answer: 57°

Example

Can 4, 6 and 11 make a triangle?

4 + 6 = 10

10 is not greater than 11

Answer: no

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Using 360° instead of 180°360° is for a full turn or a quadrilateral. A triangle has 180°.
Checking only one pair of sidesCheck that the two shortest sides add to more than the longest.
Matching the largest angle with a side next to itThe longest side is across from the largest angle.

faq.q: Why do the angles add to 180°?
faq.a: Tear off the three corners and line them up. They make a straight angle, 180°.

faq.q: Can a triangle have two right angles?
faq.a: No. Two right angles already make 180°, leaving 0° for the third.
No. 5 + 5 = 10 is not greater than 10, so the sides lie flat.

items.q: Which three lengths can make a triangle? (All lengths are in centimeters.)
items.e: The two shorter sides must add to more than the longest side: 5 + 8 = 13 > 9. So 5, 9, 8 works.

c: No, because the sides are all different
No, because 4 + 5 is not greater than 12
Yes, because any three lengths make a triangle
items.e: 4 + 5 = 9, which is not greater than 12. The two short sides cannot meet, so no triangle.
